title: Large personal Atari media, Spectrum reconstruction and 68K-tool discovery
summary: Personally screen 104 candidate URLs and add 32 projects, with two duplicate decisions and one collection exclusion.
notes: Root assistant personally performed all research and main-branch publication without a worker, PR or new branch. Twelve searches covered Atari media, C64 cartridges, Spectrum/CPC graphics, 68K analysis, PC-98 formats, Apple II development and Amiga ROM tools. Each addition has inspected implementation. Historical source, reconstruction, bytecode runtimes and translation experiments are distinguished from native ports. Older copies are linked rather than counted twice. Concrete source limits override broader README claims: atrforge modification stubs, fixed geometry, old Python syntax, machine-width assumptions and incomplete relocation proof are retained. Only explicit Claude authorship is marked; configuration alone remains unknown. No candidate code, image writer, game, emulator or firmware was executed. Upstream byte-equivalence and runtime claims remain unverified.

sources.reason: ATR filesystem reader/writer and consistency repair, ATR/IMD conversion and tokenized MAC/65 source detokenization.
6502 XEX disassembler uses memory maps, code/data/display-list sections and user symbols; PHP patcher supports game alterations.
Packages PRG files into 64KB cartridge images and CRT chip records for Magic Desk and Hucky variants.
Python port/extension parses D64, D81 and M2I, embeds cartridge loader code and constructs multi-disk EasyFlash menu banks.
Binary-derived graphics editor restoration separates the 25,856-byte core into semantic modules with cursor/input contracts, drivers and media reconstruction.
Original 1985 BASIC font editor retyped from a thermal listing with fixes and assembly helpers for 96-character font manipulation.
CharEdit/CharView handle retro text-art formats and native exports; inspected Atari output implements ANTIC display lists, XEX segments and boot ATR generation.
Browser 8x8 four-color editor packs four pixels into CPC-style bytes and exports assembly data directives.
Motorola 68000 interpreter, decoder and dynamic instruction emitter with MC68000/SCC68070 behavior profiles and C bindings.
Interactive decoder handles common Motorola 68000 instructions/addressing modes and reports estimated cycle counts.
C source implements PRG disassembly with code/data/string/table heuristics and 68000 instruction translation to C or i386 output.
Decoder exposes structured operands, symbolization and range labels with CPU-variant gating for 68000 through 68060/CPU32 and optional FPU/MMU forms.
Analyzes the European 1994 CD-i Ready release, including pregap filesystem, 521 linker symbols, executable modules, sector-aligned DAT containers, graphics and audio.
TXB unpack/repack scripts manipulate little-endian chunk offsets and compressed text blocks for translation workflows.
Qt VOL explorer/writer sources decode resource entries, sprites and PC-98 map tiles with optional trigger overlays.
Converts Spectrum screen formats including plain SCR and multi-frame Gigascreen variants into PNG/GIF imagery.
Gforth scripts translate UDG data among tape, binary-number, DEFB and Forth representations.
Converts 256x192 PBM P1/P4 images into Spectrum screen-memory ordering.
Packs/unpacks ATR images through a DIR.TXT description and filesystem implementations for Atari DOS variants, MyDOS, SpartaDOS and XDOS.
Parses ATR geometry and DOS directories with extraction, previews and evolving write operations; Go port normalizes short double-density boot sectors.
Bash/ImageMagick utility renders disk byte layout into track/sector imagery for inspection.
Converts indexed GIF graphics and SAP music to assembler data, including Atari palette approximation and compression helpers.
Extracts executable files from Homesoft-style double-density disks using a GAMES.TXT title index.
Daniel Serpell mkatr/lsatr lineage with format conversion, additional validation and reorganized CLI/documentation under Atari Foundry.
Converts PNG pixels into shifted 6502/65C02 sprite routines, with XOR/background-erasure and cycle-count generation.
Modified Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord source builds on Thomas William Ewers reverse-engineering and adds a documented body of fixes and enhancements.
High-level language interpreter/compiler emits bytecode for its own VM and includes disassembly tools on multiple 6502 machines.
Preserves Hyper-C development-system source including libraries and the BRK-entered 6502 p-code interpreter underlying its 16-bit virtual machine.
Packs directional drawing/movement commands into Applesoft shape tables with text or BLOAD-style binary output.
CLI interleaves or splits even/odd ROM parts with optional word-byte swapping and size checks.
React interface scans resident tags, inspects module layout and offers pointer/checksum patching and validation stages.
Bare-metal ROM selector firmware implements native display/input paths and device self-tests across ST/STE and selected Amiga systems.

Collection preserves third-party ATASM and utilities; inspected assembler header credits Mark Schmelzenbach. ATASM already has a dedicated tracked project. No separate independent tool identity established for this root aggregation.
Original DiagROM README explicitly marks this repository obsolete and directs readers to DiagROMV2, already tracked. Do not inflate the catalogue with the historical predecessor.

Earlier vanilla-JavaScript version of the same author’s fixed 8x8 CPC sprite editor. Inspected pixel packing and output logic match the Svelte continuation added in this batch; represent the project once.
